listing.title: Roland MS-1 Sampler
listing.description: This is the first portable sampler from Roland made in 1994. This is the precursor to the SP series which are still produced today. It was followed up by the JS-30 less than a year later, which I have another post for (8bit/16bit) The Roland MS-1 is a compact 16-bit digital phrase sampler produced from 1994 to 1997, featuring 8 rubber trigger pads, internal flash memory, and a lightweight design popular for lo-fi beats. Key Specifications & Memory Internal Memory: 384 KB holding roughly 17.8 seconds in "High" mode up to 49.2 seconds in "Long2" mode (mono). Expansion: Optional PCMCIA ATA Type II Flash RAM cards add banks C, D, and E to the built-in A and B banks. Audio Quality: Selectable sample rates/grades ranging from high fidelity down to gritty lo-fi settings. Power: Runs on 6 AA batteries or a standard DC 9V AC adapter. Workflow, Pads & Banks: 8 physical pads span 5 total banks (40 sounds maximum with a memory card inserted). Editing: Offers numerical editing for start, end, and loop points rather than visual wave markers. Sequencer: Features a basic built-in sequencer mode for real-time loop recording. This comes with the hard to find expansion card and protective pelican case. Standard 9v adapter and batteries not included. Sampler, Synthesizer, Drum Machine
